papers.title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

papers.title: Influence of stem undersizing during direct anterior approach for total hip arthroplasty on periprosthetic bone biomechanics: a finite element analysis
papers.abstract: Aims Stem undersizing during cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) may occur more frequently when the procedure is performed through the direct anterior approach (DAA) because of limited femoral exposure. Insufficient stem–bone contact may compromise primary stability and alter load transfer in the proximal femur. The aim was to investigate the biomechanical effects of femoral stem undersizing on periprosthetic bone using finite element analysis. A secondary objective was to evaluate whether the presence of a femoral stem collar modifies these biomechanical effects. Methods Patient-specific finite element models of the full femur were generated from CT data. Eight finite element models were analyzed, combining four implantation configurations of the AMIStem-P designs (Adequate Fit, Adequate Fit–Collared, Undersized, and Undersized–Collared) with two cancellous bone density conditions, representing 100% and 90% cancellous bone density. A hip joint force representing the peak loading phase during normal walking/single-leg support was applied. Strain intensity in periprosthetic trabecular bone was assessed according to Frost’s mechanostat theory, and von Mises stress distribution in the femoral stem was evaluated. Results Stem undersizing markedly increased strain intensity in the periprosthetic trabecular bone and enlarged regions exceeding the mechanostat overload threshold (> 3,000 µε). Adequate stem–bone fit with cortical support substantially reduced the volume of overloaded bone tissue. The presence of a collar reduced strain levels, particularly in undersized configurations, indicating improved proximal load transfer. Reduced cancellous bone density resulted in a moderate additional increase in strain. Simulated load reduction markedly decreased periprosthetic strain levels. Implant stresses remained well below material limits. Conclusion Femoral stem undersizing may substantially increase strain within the periprosthetic trabecular bone and enlarge regions exposed to overload conditions. Achieving adequate stem–bone fit with cortical support was associated with a marked reduction in periprosthetic bone strain. The presence of a collar appeared to partially mitigate the adverse mechanical effects of undersizing by improving proximal load transfer. Cite this article: Bone Joint Res 2026;15(11):1354–1363.

papers.title: Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. The residual is a weak space--time control-volume identity enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap, so no mesh is needed. In free-surface variables, the geometric source is integrated by parts onto the bed, so that the network is never differentiated, and a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities, located from the bathymetry alone, separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head. We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family, quadrature order and nominal bed slope, so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective; that the continuous residual characterises weak solutions; that the slope correction is consistent; and that no approximation with a continuous free surface can satisfy the head condition at a step with non-zero discharge, so that the decomposition is necessary. Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off on four lake-at-rest configurations over smooth, discontinuous, compound and tabulated beds, and the trained network reaches the equilibrium to round-off under an extended training budget. On seven Riemann problems at a bottom step, covering sub-, super- and critical transitions, the network attains relative $L^1$ free-surface errors between $6.9\times10^{-4}$ and $3.5\times10^{-3}$, and reaches critical states without prescribing them.

papers.title: FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. We introduce FanCyqlone, a linear solver that exploits parallelism across both time steps and scenario branches. The method builds on Cyqlone to compute the contribution of each branch and combines these results through a shared root problem. We integrate FanCyqlone into QPALM to develop FanCyQPALM, a solver for multi-horizon optimal control problems with general linear stage-wise constraints. We compare its performance with state-of-the-art solvers on spring-mass and quadruped control benchmarks.

papers.title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. A model trained on that naive DEL data must extrapolate to binders tighter than any it has seen, and that is where models can fail. One way to get training data with both properties is a second-generation DEL built around the hit. We ask how complex that library must be. We treat binding as a sum of small, independent interactions, called pixels on the target and antipixels on the ligand. From the spread of affinities measured in the naive library, with no structural information and nothing yet synthesized, we estimate the complexity such a library must have to supply that dense sampling and those tight binders. The method does two useful things. It turns the number of tight binders a model needs into the number of compounds a library must contain. And it estimates the expected yield of a randomly designed second-generation DEL, so the gain from designing the library with machine learning or active learning can be measured against a baseline, without the expense of a control library as large as the experiment itself.

papers.title: Capacity-Constrained Delayed Feedback for Online Conformal Risk Control
papers.abstract: Online conformal risk control (OCRC) enables reliable uncertainty quantification in machine learning by converting model outputs into prediction sets with long-term risk guarantees. These guarantees, however, hinge on the assumption that the loss of each round is revealed immediately and losslessly. In practice, feedback may be delayed, and limited resources may prevent tracking all pending predictions, causing some feedback to be lost. To address this challenge, we develop capacity-aware OCRC (CA-OCRC), a framework that jointly determines how to allocate limited tracking feedback capacity and how to construct prediction sets. CA-OCRC is based on a randomized tracking policy that samples a proxy delay to decide whether, and for how long, feedback for the current round is tracked. CA-OCRC updates the prediction sets via inverse probability weighting, compensating for the possibility of feedback lost due to delays and limited tracking capacity. We analyze risk bounds for both arbitrary and stochastic delays, revealing a trade-off between receiving more feedback and avoiding capacity saturation. Building on these bounds, we optimize the proxy delay distribution, showing scaling laws for the tracking capacity that ensure the same long-term risk as OCRC with unlimited feedback. Experiments on medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and wireless communications show the effectiveness of CA-OCRC as compared to existing OCRC mechanisms.

papers.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

papers.title: Calibration and Conformal Prediction for Medical Question Answering in Arabic and English: Evidence from Two Non-Parallel Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly tested on medical exam questions, but accuracy alone does not show when an answer can be trusted. I study the calibration and uncertainty of two open-weight models, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Jais-adapted-7B-chat (both run in 4-bit precision), on 2,816 English multiple-choice questions from MedMCQA and 4,927 Arabic multiple-choice questions from MedAraBench. Accuracy was 0.561 (English) and 0.430 (Arabic) for Qwen, and 0.369 and 0.308 for Jais. Raw option probabilities were overconfident in all four settings (expected calibration error 0.242 to 0.486), and a single temperature parameter removed 82% to 93% of that error. Split conformal prediction reached its nominal coverage in all 24 settings I tested (within 0.006), but the sets were large when accuracy was low: at 90% coverage, temperature-scaled sets contained on average 63% (Qwen, English), 78% (Qwen, Arabic), 86% (Jais, English) and 89% (Jais, Arabic) of the options. The margin between the top two option probabilities separated correct from incorrect answers best for Qwen on English (AUROC 0.734) and worst for Jais on Arabic (0.579). Answering only the 20% most confident questions lowered Qwen's English error from 0.439 to 0.098. Jais showed a strong prior for option C (49% of English and 60% of Arabic predictions). Scoring Latin letters only cut the Arabic share to 29% but left accuracy, raw ECE and AUROC nearly unchanged. Because the two benchmarks differ in subject, level and number of options, I do not attribute differences between languages to language itself. Code is available at https://github.com/Mariyaaleem/arabic-english-medqa-uncertainty.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

papers.title: Learning the Missing Derivative: Neural Multiple-Scattering Operators for Inverse Volume Rendering
papers.abstract: Reconstructing optically thick media from photographs requires modeling multiple scattering and its response to changes in extinction. Frozen-source tomography discards this derivative; differentiable path tracing estimates it through expensive, noisy sampling. We instead predict the multiple-scattering field with a neural operator and differentiate through it during inverse rendering, while computing transmittance and single scattering directly. A further challenge arises during optimization: an operator that predicts the field accurately on held-out media can still produce poor derivatives at the density states visited by the optimizer. We address this by fine-tuning on states generated during inversions driven by the operator, using Monte Carlo scattering-field supervision. On held-out optically thick clouds, our method improves relighting over frozen-source tomography at equal time and outperforms differentiable path tracing given substantially more time. Training on inversion trajectories also improves derivative alignment at visited states and reduces optimization drift.

papers.title: Rethinking Actions: Continuity-Aware Priors for World-Model Planning
papers.abstract: Actions in expert demonstrations exhibit temporal structure. An ordered-versus-shuffled analysis across five environments confirms this dependence. We ask whether action proposals that better reflect expert continuity can improve visual world-model planning. Rather than imposing generic smoothness, we learn continuations from the temporal structure of demonstrated actions. Our locality-gated deep-kernel Gaussian-process prior, LG-DKGP, combines recent and longer-range executed action history, predicts a neural continuation, and learns a temporal Gaussian-process (GP) residual. A training-derived exploration scale initializes search around the corrected mean; a frozen world model evaluates progress toward the goal. Training first fits the neural mean, then jointly optimizes the prior with the GP residual using expert future actions. The resulting planner achieves 87.07\% macro success across five simulated tasks spanning native and fragment-level goal attainment, compared with 71.03\% for INTACT, 61.66\% for PRISM, and 58.66\% for LeWM. Component interventions and expert-relative action-structure comparisons support demonstration-informed continuations and reveal task-dependent effects of visual conditioning, history length, and planning horizon.

papers.title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Gaussian process regression models are widely used in modern statistics and machine learning due to their flexibility, interpretability, built-in uncertainty quantification, and strong theoretical foundations. However, training Gaussian processes (GPs) has a computational cost of $O(n^3)$, while the memory and prediction costs are also $O(n^2)$.   For large datasets commonly encountered in practice, this becomes infeasible and necessitates the use of approximate posterior methods.   In this work, we propose a class of approximations based on sparse covariance matrices, where the kernel matrix is sparsified according to the spatial proximity of the design points.   We analyze the accuracy of the resulting approximate posterior distribution and show that the proposed approach preserves optimal statistical inference properties, provided that the dependencies among a sufficient number of neighboring points for each feature are retained.   We derive explicit sufficient and necessary conditions on the number of neighbors required in a general setting and apply these results to standard kernels, including the squared exponential and Matérn kernels. Our theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments.

papers.title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-based dexterous in-hand manipulation requires knowing not only where an object is, but also how it moves. However, most robotic manipulation systems rely on off-the-shelf visual perception models whose outputs are limited to static object masks, geometry, or 6D poses, leaving downstream controllers to infer object dynamics implicitly from noisy visual observations. We present VOKE, a kinematics-aware perception framework that augments existing object and hand-object pose estimators to recover a complete object kinematic state comprising pose, linear and angular velocity, and linear and angular acceleration. VOKE contains two core perception modules and a downstream application study. First, a Pluggable Kinematics Module (PKM) attaches to the output of a standard pose estimator and predicts the object's linear and angular velocity and acceleration from temporal visual features. Second, a Kinematics-guided Pose Refinement Module (KPRM) converts this motion vector into a second-order, motion-prior reference pose and refines the per-frame pose estimates. We evaluate VOKE on DexYCB and OakInk, where it consistently improves object pose estimation across three different backbones and substantially reduces velocity and acceleration estimation error compared with pose differencing. As a downstream application, we use Kinematics-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (KARL) to compare a kinematics-augmented policy with a pose-history baseline. After training the policies in simulation, we transfer the kinematics-augmented policy to the physical robot without policy fine-tuning, demonstrating the complete perception-to-control pathway in the target domain.

papers.title: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU
papers.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking lets a humanoid robot follow reference motions, but training a tracking policy for a library of motions has usually taken hours of GPU time. SuperMimic showed that the policy can instead be trained by backpropagating through a world model learned from parallel simulation, and InstantTrack added Muon updates, a residual policy around the reference and an averaged deployed policy. We build on both and present BlinkMimic, a recipe that makes this training faster. On a simulated Unitree G1, BlinkMimic trains one policy for all 40 LAFAN1 clips in 3.4 minutes on a single RTX 4090, measured until three consecutive checkpoints reach a normalized return of at least 0.82 with no failed clip (mean of three seeds). We split training time into the cost of an iteration, the iterations needed to fit the motions, and the iterations needed to remove the last failures, and assign each component, inherited or new, to one of these terms. The new components are a step size that decreases once training has progressed, resets directed by failures of the deployed policy under deployment conditions, and GPU graph capture of the whole iteration. A leave-one-out ablation with three seeds per component shows which term each component affects, and further measurements of the gradient, the update rule and the failure cases explain these effects. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/fuyichen0725/blinkmimic.

papers.abstract: Language models rely on finite token contexts, limiting access to earlier interactions. We introduce Recursive State-Augmented Language Models (Recursive SALM), a framework in which a persistent latent state evolves with each observation and generates adaptations of a pretrained language model. A modular read-transition-write architecture separates observation encoding, latent dynamics, and predictor adaptation. We develop deterministic and stochastic formulations.   The experiments evaluate only deterministic SALM with frozen GPT-2 small and exclude earlier evidence from its decoder context. On a four-turn hypothesis-inference task, latent-gated LoRA reaches 89.1% accuracy, comparable to 88.0% for a trained full-context LoRA baseline, with earlier evidence available solely through a 64-dimensional state. Zeroing or shuffling the state substantially reduces accuracy. In a two-turn task with codewords unseen in training, several interfaces improve candidate ranking over chance, but rarely generate the exact codeword under the evaluated training schedule. These experiments show that persistent latent-conditioned adaptation can support sequential inference when earlier evidence is absent from the decoder context.

papers.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
papers.abstract: Data-driven surrogate modeling has emerged as a powerful paradigm for accelerating computational fluid dynamics, and hierarchical U-shaped networks, which resemble the structure of classical Geometric Multigrid (GMG) methods, have become prevalent designs. Modern surrogates built on these designs achieve competitive accuracy at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers; however, accurate prediction of complex flows remains challenging, and no existing architecture leads across them. In such networks, the multigrid analogy mainly concerns the multi-resolution topology, while their components largely follow common vision practice. To address this, this study introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow fields on regular grids that spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network. Parameter-free down- and upsampling stand in for restriction and prolongation, and additive skip connections for coarse-grid correction, with normalization-free transfer and skip pathways. Within this macro-architecture, convolutions are used at the fine and intermediate resolutions and shifted-window attention at the coarsest, whose window partitioning is generalized to handle periodicity independently per axis. Evaluated on unseen test configurations across four unsteady and steady flow benchmarks against five representative baselines, SUMNO is best in 5 of 7 settings and ranks second in the remaining two. It reduces the 10-step rollout MSE by about 30% relative to the strongest baseline, and outperforms three baselines with over 130 million parameters using 9.4 million parameters.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Parallel Policy Learning for Collapse-Reactive Retreat via Hybrid Terrain Modeling
papers.abstract: At disaster sites and on unstable slopes, robot contact can collapse uninspected terrain, requiring retreat upon support loss. Massively parallel reinforcement learning of collapse-reactive retreat requires independent state--action experiences. However, on shared rigid-body collapsible terrain, one robot's collapse alters others' contacts without direct interaction. We call this indirect interference. Duplicating terrain objects prevents this but is memory-intensive, limiting parallel sampling. Our key insight is that policy learning does not necessarily require rigid-body collapse modeling, which is feasible but computationally expensive; collapse-induced contact responses can suffice. We therefore propose a memory-efficient parallel policy-learning framework for collapse-reactive retreat via hybrid terrain modeling. Hybrid terrain modeling combines rigid-body simulation of non-collapsible terrain with virtual contact forces for collapsible regions. A State-Multiplexed Contact Model shares terrain geometry and a contact-response law while maintaining environment-specific collapse states, enabling independent experiences without terrain objects for collapsible regions. The framework trains a proprioceptive policy for both normal locomotion and collapse-reactive retreat. It supports over 100 times as many parallel environments as fine-resolution rigid-block terrain within the same GPU memory limit. This scalability and improved sample efficiency enable over 50 times faster policy convergence with comparable retreat performance. Sim-to-sim and real-robot experiments demonstrate retreat under multiple collapse conditions. A supplementary video is available at: https://youtu.be/_RrhwjzEPE0

papers.title: A Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator
papers.abstract: We propose the Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator (LENO), a physics-informed neural operator for eikonal equations with heterogeneous velocity fields and general source sets. LENO encodes the variational minimum principle of viscosity solutions by constructing source-wise candidate fields and taking their pointwise minimum. This lower-envelope structure enforces the source condition exactly and represents nonsmooth multi-source solutions without a soft boundary penalty. The model is trained without precomputed solution data, using a Godunov upwind residual as the sole training signal. Experiments on point sources and curve sources, sample-dependent piecewise velocity fields, and OpenFWI CurveVel-A and Style-A media show accurate agreement with references of Fast Marching Method (FMM). Additional validation shows that the Godunov residual outperforms conventional finite difference residuals on a high-resolution test, that velocity conditioning and the lower-envelope transform are essential in realistic heterogeneous media, and that the trained operator supports efficient batched evaluation and resolution transfer.

papers.title: Engineering Vision: The Comparative Role of 3D Printing and 3D Bioprinting in Corneal Regeneration
papers.abstract: Abstract Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. Advances in additive manufacturing have positioned 3D printing and 3D bioprinting as promising platforms for fabricating anatomically informed constructs that may recapitulate key aspects of the cornea's hierarchical architecture. This review provides a mechanistic comparison of these technologies with respect to material systems and (bio)ink formulation, processing strategies, scaffold architecture, cell incorporation, and biological integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the trade-off between high-fidelity 3D-printed scaffolds that can be seeded after fabrication and cell-laden bioprinted constructs that better capture early cell-matrix interactions but remain constrained by bioink rheology, resolution, mechanical integrity, and shape retention.The review further examines emerging strategies, including decellularized extracellular matrix bioinks, functionally graded hydrogels, and hybrid electrospun-printed constructs, for improving bioactivity, structural mimicry, collagen alignment, optical transmittance, and stromal-like extracellular matrix deposition. Persistent challenges include nanoscale and membrane-like architectural replication, longterm phenotype stability, reproducible manufacturing, surgical handling, storage, and regulatory classification of combination products. By integrating material science, fabrication physics, cellular responses, and translational considerations, this review delineates the complementary roles of 3D printing and 3D bioprinting and identifies the key design criteria required to advance printed corneal constructs toward clinically translatable regeneration.

papers.title: Macroscopic plastic response and atomic-scale dislocation evolution of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ultrasonic surface rolling
papers.abstract: To address the insufficient understanding of the surface plastic deformation mechanism of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ultrasonic surface rolling processing (USRP), this study adopts an approach combining finite element (FE) simulation and molecular dynamics (MD) analysis. The effects of static load, ultrasonic vibration frequency, and ultrasonic amplitude on residual stress and surface plastic deformation are investigated, and the dislocation evolution and local deformation response under ultrasonic vibration are analyzed at the atomic scale. A three-dimensional explicit dynamic FE model based on the Johnson-Cook constitutive law is established to examine the variations of surface residual stress, equivalent plastic strain, and plastic displacement under different static loads, ultrasonic vibration frequencies, and ultrasonic amplitudes, and the validity of the FE model is verified against experimentally measured residual stress results. The results show that static load is the dominant factor governing the degree of macroscopic surface plastic deformation. Within the investigated static-load range of 100–400 N, the magnitude of the peak residual compressive stress increases overall from 685.11 MPa to 722.09 MPa, although the variation is not strictly monotonic, while the maximum PEEQ increases from 0.12481 to 0.38641 and the affected depths increase markedly. Increasing the ultrasonic amplitude further enhances near-surface plastic deformation, whereas the influence of ultrasonic vibration frequency on macroscopic plastic deformation is relatively limited within the 20–29 kHz range. On this basis, a simplified Ti-Al atomic model of the α phase of Ti-6Al-4V alloy is established to analyze the effect of ultrasonic vibration on atomic-scale plastic deformation behavior by comparing the dislocation evolution, loading force, and system potential energy under conditions with and without ultrasonic vibration. The MD results indicate that periodic excitation is accompanied by an increase in the number and total line length of detected dislocations, together with lower time-averaged indentation reaction forces and higher reported potential-energy values under the investigated simulation conditions. These observations suggest that periodic excitation modifies local defect evolution and indentation response within the simplified atomic model, providing complementary insights into atomic-scale plastic deformation. This study can provide a reference for process optimization and surface strengthening mechanism research of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during USRP.

papers.title: A weak-form discrete physical-residual PINN method for solving multigroup neutron diffusion equations
papers.abstract: To address the substantial computational burden of high-order spatial derivatives, the difficulty of residual optimization near material interfaces, and the optimization stiffness associated with direct space-time training when conventional strong-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are applied to heterogeneous multigroup neutron diffusion problems, a PINN method based on weak-form discrete physical residuals is developed. Finite-element shape functions are used to construct the flux interpolation field and assemble the discrete physical operators, while the neural network predicts nodal fluxes and neural source iteration drives the coupled convergence of the fluxes and effective multiplication factor. P1 triangular elements are adopted for the two-dimensional problem and Q1 hexahedral elements for the three-dimensional problem, eliminating the need to evaluate high-order spatial derivatives of the flux by automatic differentiation during training. The method is progressively verified using the TWIGL and IAEA-3D PWR benchmarks. For the steady-state TWIGL problem, the PINN yields an effective multiplication factor of 0.9132141, differing from the finite element method (FEM) result by 0.04 pcm, while the root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of both fast- and thermal-group fluxes are below 2.4 × 10 −4 . When this steady-state flux is used to initialize the FEM/Crank–Nicolson (C-N) transient calculation, the RMSEs of relative power for the step and ramp perturbations are 5.27 × 10 −4 and 4.57 × 10 −4 , respectively, relative to the pure FEM/C-N results; the maximum absolute relative deviations from the published POLCA-T reference values are both below 0.1%. For the IAEA-3D PWR problem, the PINN produces an effective multiplication factor of 1.0289669, differing from the same-mesh FEM result by 3.67 pcm. The RMSEs of the fast- and thermal-group fluxes are 3.008 × 10 −3 and 1.487 × 10 −3 , respectively. For the assembly relative power, the mean and maximum absolute relative errors with respect to published reference values are 0.1779% and 0.4647%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method avoids the dependence of strong-form PINNs on high-order spatial automatic differentiation and achieves accurate solutions of heterogeneous two-dimensional P1 and three-dimensional Q1 multigroup core-diffusion problems within a unified framework, providing a common methodological basis for differentiable solution of complex reactor-physics problems.

papers.title: Phased Array Antenna Surface Deformation Reconstruction Based on Modal Low-Rank Correction and Gaussian Process Data Migration
papers.abstract: Deformation of a phased array antenna surface can degrade its electrical performance. Conventional modal reconstruction depends on the accuracy of the structural model, while purely data-driven methods require extensive experimental data. We propose a reconstruction method that combines a modal prior, an input-dependent low-rank correction network, and Gaussian process data migration. Finite element modal analysis informs the baseline strain-to-displacement mapping. The correction network adapts this mapping to the input strain. Gaussian processes trained on experimental displacement residuals generate pseudo-experimental labels and confidence weights for fine-tuning. In the panel case study, the proposed method achieved a mean absolute error of 0.1596 mm and a maximum absolute error of 0.5963 mm. The corresponding errors for the conventional modal method were 1.5922 mm and 5.7291 mm. The proposed method retains an explicit strain-to-displacement mapping and uses a small experimental dataset.

papers.title: Embedded 3D Bioprinting for Perfusable Vascular Networks: Supporting-Bath Materials, Structural Fidelity, and Functional Validation
papers.abstract: Vascularization remains the principal bottleneck preventing engineered tissues from reaching clinically relevant thickness, and conventional extrusion printing cannot reconcile the low-viscosity, cell-rich bioinks required for biological function with the mechanical support needed to build suspended, branched, and hollow architectures. Embedded bioprinting resolves this conflict by transferring structural support from the ink to a yield-stress bath that locally fluidizes around the moving needle and self-heals behind it, thereby decoupling printability from ink rheology. This review presents a unified parameter-to-function analysis of extrusion-based embedded bioprinting for perfusable vascular networks. We first classify support baths along two orthogonal dimensions—post-printing fate (temporary support versus retained matrix) and physical form (granular, continuous-phase, or liquid)—and distill their behavior into four coupled rheological descriptors: yield stress, shear thinning, thixotropic recovery, and storage modulus. These parameters, together with ink–bath compatibility and process conditions, are then linked to structural fidelity in both its static (geometric accuracy) and dynamic (shape retention during crosslinking and culture) senses, and reported failure modes are consolidated into a parameter–defect–countermeasure matrix. Vascular fabrication strategies are organized into sacrificial-lumen and functional-ink direct-writing routes, and the strength of published validation is appraised through a three-level evidence framework spanning structural patency, biological maturation, and direct function, with direct embedded evidence explicitly separated from benchmarks borrowed from adjacent technologies. Persistent challenges—including the resolution gap relative to capillary dimensions, bath removal and residue control, non-transferable rheological windows, and the scarcity of long-term and interlaboratory functional data—are critically examined. Finally, we outline priorities in closed-loop intelligent process control, function-oriented design, tunable and responsive support baths, hybrid fabrication, and standardized quantitative reporting, charting a path from printable structures to predictable vascular function.

papers.title: A patient-derived, autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel system for lung cancer organoid culture and recapitulation of immunotherapy response
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Matrigel-based culture of patient-derived lung cancer organoids (LCOs) is limited by undefined composition, batch-to-batch variability, and immunogenicity, which compromise experimental reproducibility and drug response readouts. Methods: We developed an autologous component-integrated hydrogel by incorporating patient-derived decellularized lung fiber fragments (1.25 μm diameter; 52.5 μm length) and optimized autologous plasma (56 °C, 30 min; 8,000×g, 5 min; 5% v/v) into a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) network. Five formulations—GelMA, GelMA+ fiber, GelMA + plasma, MC-GelMA (fibers + plasma) and Matrigel—were compared to dissect component contributions. LCOs were established from 8 patients, and PBMC co-culture experiments were performed with 3 samples (1 PD-L1-positive, 2 PD-L1-negative). Results: MC-GelMA exhibited uniform porosity and a Young’s modulus of 15.67 ± 0.86 kPa, closely matching native lung tumor tissue. Compared with Matrigel, LCOs cultured in MC-GelMA exhibited in vivo-like morphology, enhanced viability and metabolic activity, and preservation of key histological and genomic features.The platform supported stable long-term culture through passage 9 with maintained drug sensitivity. Component analysis revealed that fibers mainly provided structural and mechanical cues, while plasma supplied biochemical signals; their combination synergistically enhanced organoid growth and immune cell infiltration. In co-culture, MC-GelMA recapitulated anti-PD-L1 responses: PD-L1-positive organoids showed increased LDH release, whereas PD-L1-negative organoids did not respond. Conclusion: In conclusion, this autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel serves as a highly reproducible biofabrication platform for stable LCO culture and reliable recapitulation of patient-specific immunotherapy response patterns. Further validation in larger cohorts is warranted to establish its predictive potential for clinical immunotherapy outcomes.

papers.title: Pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface coordinates infection control and osseointegration
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) compromises osseointegration through bacterial colonisation and dysregulated inflammation. Here, we pre-established a living biointerface by seeding immunity-and-matrix-regulatory cells (IMRCs) onto three-dimensional (3D)-printed titanium prostheses modified with silver (Ag) by plasma immersion ion implantation (Ag-PIII) before bacterial exposure, generating an IMRC-seeded Ag-PIII-modified titanium (TAM) construct. TAM was associated with reduced bacterial attachment. The Ag-PIII-modified substrate achieved antibacterial efficiencies above 99% against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli while supporting IMRC viability and attachment. TAM-conditioned medium favoured an M2-like macrophage profile, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In the beagle PJI model, TAM reduced bacterial recovery and peri-implant inflammation and improved bone formation, fixation strength, and locomotor performance at 8 weeks. These findings provide preclinical support for pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface to alter the initial conditions of surface competition and integrate early infection control with subsequent osseointegration.

papers.title: A study on the 3D printing preparation method of reinforced casings for lithium-ion batteries in energy storage power stations using high specific energy absorption metamaterials
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing has enabled the development of advanced lattice and metamaterial structures with tailored mechanical performance for energy absorption and lightweight structural applications. In this study, a novel round gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) metamaterial is designed, fabricated 3D printing, and systematically investigated under quasi-static compression loading. A combined experimental and finite element method (FEM) approach is employed to evaluate the mechanical response and validate the numerical model. The FEM results show excellent agreement with experiments, with only 1.3% deviation in stiffness and 5.8% difference in ultimate compressive load, confirming the high accuracy of the developed simulation framework in capturing the complex deformation behavior of the proposed architecture. The deformation analysis reveals a progressive and stable collapse mechanism governed by distributed plasticity and strain localization within the gyroid network. A comprehensive parametric study is then conducted to investigate the influence of structure thickness (T) and unit-cell height (H) on mechanical performance. The results demonstrate that T is the dominant parameter controlling load-bearing capacity and energy absorption, while H mainly influences deformation evolution with limited impact on global response. Importantly, the structure exhibits exceptionally high specific energy absorption (SEA), reaching up to 2586.5 mJ/g, significantly increasing with thickness and showing only minor variation (1–3%) with changes in H. This highlights the robustness and tunability of the proposed design for energy dissipation applications. Overall, the findings confirm that the proposed round gyroid TPMS metamaterial introduces a new geometry-driven strategy for achieving high-performance, lightweight, and highly efficient energy-absorbing structures.

papers.title: Immune-instructive biofabrication for musculoskeletal tissue regeneration
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal repair requires coordinated tissue organization and host responses that evolve across space and time. Immune-instructive biofabrication aims to use material and manufacturing design to create reproducible biological exposures that influence host function and support regeneration. This narrative review clarifies the distinction between immune association, modulation, regulation, and instruction, and considers how biofabrication choices may shape immune-regenerative interactions across musculoskeletal tissues. Current evidence is organized around the location, timing, agent, and functional dose of manufactured cues, together with the multicellular networks involved in healing. Although engineered constructs can influence inflammatory responses while supporting tissue repair, direct evidence linking specific manufacturing features to causal immune mechanisms and durable function remains limited. Progress will require appropriately matched controls, spatial and longitudinal assessment, mechanistic testing, tissue-relevant functional outcomes, and standardized potency measures. This framework provides a basis for designing and evaluating musculoskeletal biofabrication strategies that integrate structural reconstruction with controlled host-response modulation.

papers.title: Multivariate Gaussian process emulation for multifidelity computer models with high-dimensional spatial outputs
papers.abstract: Risk assessment of hurricane-driven storm surge relies on deterministic computer models that produce outputs over a large spatial domain. The surge models can often be run at a range of fidelity levels, with greater precision yielding more accurate simulations. Improved accuracy comes with a significant increase in computational expense, necessitating the development of an emulator which leverages information from the more plentiful low-fidelity outputs to provide fast and accurate predictions of high-fidelity simulations. To properly assess the risk of storm surge over a geographic region at aggregated spatial resolution, an emulator must account for spatial dependence between outputs yet remain computationally feasible for high-dimensional simulations. To address this challenge, we exploit the autoregressive cokriging framework to develop two cross-covariance structures to account for spatial dependence. One approach uses a separable covariance structure with a sparse Cholesky prior for the inverse of the cross-covariance matrix; the other involves a low-rank approximation via basis representations. We demonstrate their predictive performance in the storm surge application and a testbed example.

papers.title: Computationally efficient estimation of localized treatment effects for multi-level, multi-component interventions to address the opioid crisis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The opioid epidemic remains a major public health challenge in the United States, requiring a multi-pronged intervention approach to mitigate harms to communities. Given the heterogeneity of the epidemic, it is crucial for policymakers to understand localized treatment effects of different intervention components and utilize limited resources efficiently. While locally calibrated simulation models can project epidemic outcomes for any given intervention policy, collecting simulation results for all intervention combinations to estimate localized treatment effects for each community is impractical because the number of combinations grows exponentially with the number of interventions and the levels at which they are applied. To tackle this, we develop a two-stage metamodel framework with a two-step sequential design for efficient sampling. The metamodel consists of a response function linking health out-comes to each intervention component’s treatment effect, and a Gaussian process regression (GPR) to learn spatial and socio-economic structures of the treatment effects based on locally-contextualized covariates. With two-step sequential sampling, we leverage spatial correlations and posterior uncertainty to sequentially sample the most informative counties and treatment conditions. We apply this framework to estimate the treatment effects of buprenorphine dispensing and naloxone distribution on overdose mortality rates using a calibrated agent-based opioid epidemic model in Pennsylvania counties. Our approach achieves less than 5% average relative error using fewer than 2% of the runs required for an exhaustive simulation. Our two-stage framework provides a computationally efficient approach to support policymakers, enabling an efficient evaluation of alternative resource-allocation strategies to mitigate the opioid epidemic in local communities.

papers.title: Towards spatio-temporal extrapolation of phase-field simulations with convolution-only neural networks
papers.abstract: Phase-field simulations of liquid metal dealloying (LMD) capture complex microstructural evolution but become prohibitively expensive over large domains and long time horizons. We introduce a fully convolutional, conditionally parameterized U-Net surrogate designed to extrapolate far beyond its training data in both space and time. The architecture combines convolutional self-attention, physically informed padding, and a flood-fill corrector to preserve accuracy under extrapolation, while conditioning on simulation parameters enables flexible time-step skipping and adaptation to varying alloy compositions. To eliminate the need for costly solver-based initialization, we couple the surrogate with a conditional diffusion model that generates synthetic, physically consistent initial conditions. Training uses simulations on small domains over short time spans; exploiting the convolutional nature of U-Nets, the trained surrogate then runs and extrapolates to longer horizons than classical numerical solvers can reach. Across multiple alloy compositions, the framework reproduces LMD physics accurately within the spatial and temporal ranges validated against direct numerical simulation (DNS). It predicts key quantities of interest and spatial statistics with relative errors typically below 5% in the training regime and under 15% during large-scale, long-horizon extrapolation. The framework delivers speed-ups of $${{{\mathcal{O}}}}(1{0}^{4})$$ over DNS, reducing weeks-long simulations to seconds and allowing the computational domain to expand beyond what conventional mesh-based discretizations permit. This work is a first stepping stone toward surrogate models for rapid screening, parameter studies, and uncertainty quantification in LMD.

papers.title: Advancements in Fused Deposition Modeling: Materials, Processes, and Emerging Trends in Polymer Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) has become a leading technology in polymer additive manufacturing due to its versatility, cost effectiveness, and accessibility. This review explores the current advancements, material innovations, and emerging trends within FDM, particularly focusing on high performance polymers and composite materials. Key materials like PEEK (Polyetheretherketone), PEI (Polyetherimide), and PPSU (Polyphenylsulfone) are discussed in terms of their mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, as well as their applications across industries such as aerospace, automotive, and medical devices. The incorporation of fiber and particle reinforced composites has significantly enhanced FDM capabilities, offering improved strength, rigidity, and thermal resistance for demanding applications. Moreover, the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to revolutionize the FDM process by enabling predictive maintenance, and real time monitoring. However, challenges such as printability, cost, and material limitations continue to hinder broader adoption, especially for high performance composites and advanced materials. The review concludes by highlighting areas for future research, and material development, which are essential for unlocking the full potential of FDM in both prototyping and end use production.

papers.abstract: Periodic sensorless finite-control-set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) evaluates all eight voltage vectors every 10μs, even when the applied vector is still adequate. This study develops a controller that reuses the applied vector when one held-vector prediction satisfies the descent and current constraints. A double-power saturated sliding-mode observer supplies position and speed, and its sliding residual tightens or relaxes the descent threshold. Under bounded lumped disturbances, the sliding error reaches a prescribed boundary layer in bounded time, while the compensated-current error remains locally uniformly ultimately bounded. At the largest simulated initial error, the double-power law shortens boundary-layer entrance from 2.11 to 1.08 ms and post-load-step speed-estimation recovery from 55.23 to 24.35 ms. Across the composite profile, 39.42% of periods require full enumeration, reducing candidate-state checks by 60.6%. With a similar update budget, position RMSE falls from 1.035∘ to 0.949∘. On the hardware bench, full-enumeration checks fall by 21.6% and equivalent switching frequency by 14.9%; speed-tracking and electrical-angle RMSE increase by 1.22r/min and 0.400∘, respectively. These measurements show the computational saving and its accuracy cost.

papers.title: Study on Static–Dynamic Characteristics and Decoupling of Agricultural Heavy-Load Six-Dimensional Force Sensor Based on Improved XGBoost Model
papers.abstract: Precision operation is one of the crucial means to reduce costs and consumption in the agricultural production process. To enhance the operational efficiency of machinery, combined operation machines are often used for tillage operations. A large unbalanced inertial load is caused during operation, which also exhibit features such as continuity and uncertainty. A six-dimensional force sensor can simultaneously test and output six types of load information, which is an effective means for intelligent detection. However, inter-dimensional coupling of the sensor is unavoidable. Most existing studies on the static and dynamic characteristics as well as decoupling of six-dimensional force sensors are conducted for light-load and low-interference scenarios, which cannot be applied to farmland tillage scenarios characterized by heavy load and high interference. In this paper, focusing on the heavy-load working conditions of the six-dimensional force sensor, static and dynamic calibration tests based on full-scale force and torque loading were carried out to analyze the static and dynamic characteristic indicators of the six-dimensional force sensor. Additionally, research on static and dynamic decoupling of the six-dimensional force sensor based on the improved XGBoost model was conducted, and the decoupling effect of the improved XGBoost model was verified. The test results show the following: (1) The BO-XG Boost model based on Bayesian optimization exhibited superior performance. Compared with the conventional XGBoost model, the improved XGBoost model reduced the tuning time by 35.5% and achieved a lower RMSE. (2) The decoupling performance of the improved XG Boost model was significantly superior to that of Light GBM. When the loading frequency condition was 20 Hz, the R2P values of Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My and Mz were increased by 1.77%, 3.12%, 10.67%, 1.36%, 0.16%, and 0.18% respectively. At a loading frequency condition of 40 Hz, the R2P values of the six types of loads were improved by 0.78%, 0.72%, 0.90%, 0.50%, 1.77%, and 0.55% respectively, with corresponding improvements observed at other frequencies. When the loading frequency condition was 160 Hz, the R2P values of Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My and Mz all exceed 0.99. The improved XGBoost model could significantly reduce the coupling of electrical signals from other channels to the main channel, making it suitable for the dynamic decoupling of this sensor.

papers.abstract: Purpose Forecasting soybean oil prices is difficult because price movements emerge from interacting supply, demand, inventory, trade and macro-financial forces, especially in import-dependent markets where external shocks can rapidly alter conditions. This study develops a comparative framework for integrating economic theory into physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for soybean oil price forecasting. Design/methodology/approach These constraints are examined through five artificial neural network (ANN)-based models: a baseline ANN, PINN-A, PINN-B, PINN-C and a unified PINN-ABC model, evaluated not only for predictive performance but also for forecast robustness, interpretability and structural consistency. Findings Embedding economic theory into PINNs improves forecasting, but its effectiveness depends on the type of constraint imposed. Constraints that directly encode economically interpretable directional relationships contribute most, while combining multiple constraints creates trade-offs between structural richness and optimisation complexity. Research limitations/implications Economics-guided PINNs offer a promising bridge between flexible neural forecasting and theory-consistent commodity market analysis, supporting forecasts that are accurate, economically credible and decision-relevant. Originality/value Rather than treating forecasting as a purely data-driven task, the study conceptualises economic theory as the analogue of “physics”, embedding structurally meaningful economic relationships directly into the neural learning objective as soft constraints. Three forms of economic structure are incorporated: bounded short-run adjustment and temporal smoothness, equilibrium correction and monotonic responses to key fundamentals.

papers.title: Exact prevalence regions: finite-sample uncertainty quantification, threshold decisions, and monitoring for class-prevalence analytics under prior probability shift
papers.abstract: Abstract Many analytics decisions consume class prevalences rather than individual labels: the market share of a sentiment, the case burden of a disease, the drift state of a deployed model. Quantification methods estimate the prevalence vector of an unlabeled batch under prior probability shift, but they return point estimates, and their uncertainty companions, resting on large-sample approximations, resampling, or a prior, carry no finite-sample frequentist guarantee. I introduce exact prevalence regions (EPR): confidence regions obtained by inverting exact Monte Carlo two-sample tests against reference samples drawn from held-out, class-conditional calibration pools. Because prior probability shift makes each null hypothesis exactly simulable, the region is finite-sample valid for any classifier, any permutation-symmetric statistic, and any sample size, marginally over calibration sampling; the exchangeability the test uses is derived from the sampling assumptions, and the cost of its failure under within-batch dependence is measured. The same construction yields exact one-sided tests for threshold decisions and a day-over-day monitoring workflow whose representability alarm flags batches that leave the label-shift family. Across 18 datasets and more than 300,000 evaluation bags, against audited bootstrap, delta-method, and Bayesian baselines, EPR held its nominal level wherever the shift assumption held by construction, including 0.950 on all 5000 official bags of the 28-class LeQua 2022 task, where bootstrap coverage spanned 0.030–0.974 across implementations and seeds. The cost is width, 1.13–1.43 times the delta method’s outside rare-class regimes, and reduced power in threshold decisions; both are quantified and distilled into practitioner guidance.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogate for Two-Dimensional Field Prediction in a Steam Methane Reforming Reactor
papers.abstract: Steam methane reforming (SMR) is an important industrial reaction. Process simulation tools such as Aspen and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are widely used to model it and perform well under specific operating conditions. However, when operating conditions vary and repeated calculations are required, the computational time cost becomes high. Neural networks can make fast data-driven predictions, but purely data-driven models may produce results that violate physical laws. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine data-driven prediction with physical equations, using the governing partial differential equations as constraints during training to improve physical consistency. In this work, a dual-network PINN was trained on 400 of 520 numerical reference conditions, with 60 conditions used for validation and 60 for testing. The trained PINN achieves mean casewise RMSEs of 3.08 K for bed temperature and 0.0053 bar for pressure, with a recorded reference-to-PINN evaluation-time ratio of approximately 1.81×104. Within the investigated operating range, RBF interpolation and ordinary Kriging achieved lower prediction and balance errors and shorter prediction times than the PINN, whose inlet-region temperature accuracy remains a limitation.

papers.abstract: Distributed drive heavy-duty vehicles with four-wheel independent driving and steering offer superior maneuverability, but their large mass and high center of gravity make them prone to rollover during cornering. Since lateral and roll motions are inherently coupled through lateral acceleration, yet existing path tracking controllers generally treat them separately and rely on fixed weightings, this study aims to coordinate path tracking and roll stability simultaneously. A reduced-order six-state prediction model is developed to explicitly capture the lateral–roll coupling, and a Nash bargaining game-based model predictive control strategy is proposed, in which two virtual players sharing the same control inputs are coordinated through a Pareto-optimal bargaining solution. A roll risk indicator-driven safety mapping law then adaptively adjusts the game weight online, forming a dual-layer protection architecture of game optimality plus safety coverage. TruckSim–MATLAB/Simulink co-simulation under extreme maneuvers shows that, compared with a tracking-only MPC, the proposed strategy maintains tracking accuracy while reducing the peak roll risk indicator by 45.2% and the maximum roll angle by 12.4%. The maximum absolute load transfer ratio is reduced from 1.0000 to 0.8944, so that the inner wheels remain clear of lift-off throughout the maneuver. The adaptive weight confirms the intended tracking-priority and stability-priority behavior, achieving a Pareto-optimal trade-off between the two objectives.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Simulation-Based Optimization for Low-Carbon Traffic Signal Control in Large-Scale Urban Networks
papers.abstract: Large-scale urban traffic signal optimization presents substantial challenges arising from high-dimensional decision spaces, expensive microscopic simulations, and competing mobility and environmental objectives. This study formulates large-scale traffic signal timing as a high-dimensional bi-objective black-box optimization problem, in which average waiting time and total CO2 emissions are minimized simultaneously, thereby ensuring a symmetric and preference-neutral treatment of the two conflicting objectives without imposing predefined preference weights. To address the computational challenges, a Pareto–Hypervolume Guided Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization (PHV-TuRBO) method is proposed. The framework integrates Pareto-guided center selection, exploiting front sparsity and surrogate uncertainty, with hypervolume-driven trust-region adaptation to balance exploration and exploitation under limited simulation budgets. Experiments on 100-dimensional DTLZ1 and DTLZ2 benchmarks demonstrate superior convergence and Pareto-front approximation compared with NSGA-II, ParEGO, qEHVI-MOBO, and MORBO. Further validation on a large-scale Beijing traffic network involving 456 continuous decision variables and a budget of 5000 simulator evaluations demonstrates the effectiveness of PHV-TuRBO in identifying diverse efficiency–emission trade-offs. Representative Pareto-optimal solutions achieve substantial improvements in waiting time, travel time, queue length, stop frequency, mean speed, and CO2 emissions relative to the original signal plan. These results establish PHV-TuRBO as a sample-efficient approach to high-dimensional, multi-objective traffic signal optimization for sustainable urban mobility.

papers.title: Bayesian Sound Source Localisation of Aerial-Hawking Bats Using an Array of Synchronised Passive Acoustic Monitors
papers.abstract: Monitoring animals from their vocalisations has proven indispensable for ecological research, with applications ranging from unbiased population estimation for biodiversity assessment to kinematic and acoustic quantification for research into evolutionary adaptation. Near-field sound source localisation techniques infer the location of vocalising animals by estimating the signal propagation delay across a spatially distributed array of passive acoustic monitors using either the times of arrival (ToA) or time differences of arrival (TDoA). As with all real-world measurements, ToA and TDoA estimates are subject to noise and uncertainty, particularly for ultrasonic sounds. With the development of low-cost synchronised passive acoustic monitors, many of the historical logistical barriers to deploying receiver arrays for sound source localisation have been ameliorated. Yet, the problems of uncertainty quantification, robustness, and open availability of analysis software remain core challenges to the greater adoption of sound source localisation in ecological research. In this paper, we address these existing limitations by considering a Bayesian approach to sound source localisation and trajectory estimation of the aerial-hawking common pipistrelle bat (Pipistrellus pipistrellus). We estimate the posterior distribution of ultrasonic echolocation call source locations via a general-purpose Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampler, extending this model to infer continuous flight trajectories using a smooth Gaussian process prior. The resulting tool effectively captures measurement uncertainty, producing a principled probabilistic estimate of sound source localisation. We validate the model through simulation-based calibration checking and demonstrate the efficacy of this approach for field deployment using an array of five GPS-synchronised AudioMoth receivers to track free flying bats, achieving a median predicted precision of 25cm. Our approach has the potential to improve bat population estimates from passive acoustic data.

papers.title: Beyond governing-equation residuals: verification and validation of physics-informed neural networks for forward structural-dynamic response prediction
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks are increasingly explored for forward structural-dynamic response prediction because governing mechanics can be embedded directly in learning. Satisfying those equations, however, does not establish that a predicted response is numerically reliable or physically credible. Structural dynamics impose further verification and validation (VandV) demands involving derivative-dependent engineering quantities, long-duration responses, frequency and modal behavior, changing operating conditions, and the provenance of the reference used for comparison. Existing PINN reviews identify many of these issues, but they have not provided a study-level audit of how the corresponding evidence is distributed across published forward structural dynamic studies. This Mini Review addresses that gap. Drawing on established computational mechanics VandV practice, we define four evidence dimensions: equation and numerical consistency, structural response verification, dynamic fidelity, and predictive scope with benchmark provenance. Each dimension is resolved into categories with explicit decision rules. These rules are then applied through a full-text review of a delimited study corpus. Each dimension is tied to measurable evidence and to a reporting chain connecting the quantity of interest, the error metric, the reference and its uncertainty, the intended-use tolerance, the observed error, and the resulting VandV conclusion. The resulting evidence map shows that validation coverage remains uneven and that evidence is rarely accumulated across dimensions within individual studies. Worked applications further show that the dimensions complement rather than substitute for one another. Credible forward structural-dynamics PINNs therefore require mechanics-relevant, purpose-specific validation beyond residual minimization or isolated agreement in displacement.

papers.title: Accelerating the Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

The pitch dynamics are embedded in the offline training loss as a physical constraint. During control operation, the trained PINN is evaluated at the current inputs with fixed weights and biases, and its predictions update the inverse model and control effectiveness terms. The RBF network provides online residual compensation. The PINN captures the trends of the pitching moment coefficient and its aerodynamic derivatives, providing model information for dynamic inversion. Compared with the implemented fixed-gain PID baseline, the model-informed controllers reduce angle-of-attack tracking errors and transient overshoot under the prescribed simulation conditions. RBF compensation further reduces the remaining tracking deviations. These results concern the prescribed numerical tracking test; they do not establish flight safety, loss-of-control prevention, emergency stall recovery, or performance on a civil aircraft. The stability result is conditional on a bounded operating region, a uniformly bounded residual, effective control authority, and the stated actuator realization conditions.

papers.title: Hilberg's law as learning a world state: implications and limits for text compression
papers.abstract: Hilberg's hypothesis states that block entropy of text grows as hn + An^beta. We connect maximal entropy random walk (Parry) sequence ensembles, ANS-like equipartition of surprisal, Santa Fe processes with an HCR-motivated Gaussian world model, and LLM-based entropy measurements into a picture of text as progressive revelation of a world state. Calibration on Santa Fe processes shows that PPMd compression slopes barely respond to the true Hilberg exponent, while a word-level Pitman-Yor coder recovers it but measures lexicon occupancy. A permutation-calibrated lexical index detects word-order effects in anthologies. For compression, a self-contained coder cannot remove a genuine An^beta source term; explicit word and recency models reduce predictive log loss by 1.5-3.4% over a context-mixing base, and shared dictionaries pay off mainly for small independently coded documents. Supplementary files contain all code and results.

papers.title: Destination-Reserve-Aware Eco-MPC for Autonomous Battery Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: Short-horizon ecological model predictive control (Eco-MPC) coordinates energy use and car-following performance for battery electric vehicles (BEVs), whereas a destination-reserve target imposes a trip-level energy requirement. This paper proposes a destination-reserve-aware Eco-MPC that feeds remaining-trip energy adequacy into short-horizon car-following control through an outer supervisor. The supervisor blends prior and observed energy intensity to estimate remaining demand and activates a distance-indexed net-energy budget under reserve risk. A bounded energy account carries short-term budget deviations across updates. SUMO experiments include deterministic mechanism and remaining-demandestimation sensitivity analyses and paired held-out stochastic comparisons with fixed-weight and reserve-triggered adaptive-weight Eco-MPCs. At the lowest tested initial-energy level, deterministic trip energy decreased by 5.0% with a 1.2-s trip-time increase, improving the terminal reserve margin from -38.7 to -0.32 Wh. At the same initial-energy level, across three stochastic traffic conditions, mean terminal reserve margin increased by 27.2–45.5 Wh relative to fixed-weight control. Energy intensity decreased by 5.0–8.3 Wh/km, while trip time increased by 3.7–5.6 s. Relative to the specified adaptive-weight comparator, mean energy intensity decreased by 2.0–4.2 Wh/km and trip time shortened by 1.9–3.1 s. Controller differences generally diminished as initial energy increased, indicating that the proposed reserve regulation responds to the level of available trip energy.

papers.title: A Localized Basis Structure in Physics-Informed Neural Network for Solving Elliptic Problems
papers.abstract: We present physics-informed neural network (PINN) approaches for solving elliptic boundary value problems with improved stability and accuracy. Standard PINNs based on multilayer perceptrons often exhibit limited approximation power and unstable convergence, particularly when trained with second-order optimization methods. To overcome these issues, we propose a family of localized basis-inspired architectures specifically designed to work effectively with the Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) optimizer. The Localized Basis Net (LBN) employs localized units with interpretable parameters, the extended LBN (XLBN) augments this structure with nonlinear mixing for enhanced flexibility, and the Fixed Basis Net (FBN) is a variant of XLBN where basis-related parameters are fixed to isolate and evaluate the effect of learning basis functions. We also establish the approximation capability of LBNs in Sobolev norms. Numerical experiments show that the proposed networks, when coupled with LM, achieve robust convergence and higher accuracy for a variety of elliptic problems, including linear, multiscale coefficient, and nonlinear p-Laplacian equations. These results demonstrate that network–optimizer co-design provides a promising direction for developing reliable and interpretable neural network methods in scientific computing.

papers.title: Conformalized Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Abstract To investigate whether conformal prediction (CP)-based uncertainty quantification (UQ) can improve semi-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks. Five machine learning (ML) frameworks were developed and evaluated: supervised learning (SL), standard SSL, iterative SSL, conformalized SSL (CSSL), and iterative CSSL. Logistic regression (LR) models were trained using radiomics features extracted from MRI and CT datasets across three classification tasks: isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation prediction in gliomas, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation prediction in gliomas, and histopathological classification in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) with 95% confidence intervals, and statistical comparisons were performed using DeLong’s test. Across all three tasks, uncertainty-aware SSL frameworks outperformed conventional SL and standard SSL approaches. For IDH prediction, CSSL and iterative CSSL demonstrated statistically significant improvements compared with SL and SSL ( p < 0.05). For MGMT prediction, iterative SSL, CSSL, and iterative CSSL significantly outperformed SL ( p < 0.05). Similarly, in NSCLC histology classification, iterative SSL and CSSL-based methods significantly improved performance compared with SL ( p < 0.05). Integrating CP into SSL frameworks improves pseudo-label reliability by filtering uncertain predictions and reducing error propagation during self-training. The proposed uncertainty-aware SSL approaches demonstrated improved performance across multiple radiomics-based classification tasks, highlighting their potential utility in medical imaging applications where labeled data are limited but unlabeled data are abundant.
