papers.title: Application of a hybrid GR4J-PINNS framework for enhanced extreme flood peak simulation in a tropical Monsoon Basin, Vietnam
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Conceptual rainfall–runoff models such as GR4J provide a parsimonious and physically interpretable framework for streamflow simulation, but their accuracy may decline during extreme floods in tropical monsoon catchments with concentrated rainfall and nonlinear runoff responses. This study presents a hybrid GR4J–Physics-Informed Neural Network (GR4J–PINNs) framework to improve flood-peak simulation while preserving the physical interpretability of GR4J. The calibrated GR4J model is treated as a frozen physical trajectory, while a neural network learns the residual error between simulated and observed discharge under a physics-consistency constraint that penalizes departures from the mass-conservative GR4J solution. To address data scarcity in the Vu Gia–Thu Bon River Basin, Vietnam, the framework incorporates NASA GLDAS satellite-derived evapotranspiration and a regression-based baseflow index derived from Lyne–Hollick filtering without using observed discharge as an input. Using a chronological train/test partition (2010–2020) and a prospective application trial (2021–2022), GR4J–PINNs improves NSE from 0.882 to 0.967 and R2 from 0.939 to 0.983, while reducing MAE and RMSE by 61.8 and 46.7%, respectively. The results demonstrate improved flood-peak simulation and robust performance, highlighting GR4J–PINNs as a non-intrusive, auditable approach for integrating conceptual hydrological models with deep learning in data-scarce tropical basins.

papers.title: Time-aware evaluation of metaheuristic-optimized support vector regression for permeate conductivity in hybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis desalination
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine learning models of desalination plants are often tested on random splits of time-ordered records, which can overstate their accuracy. This study evaluated support vector regression (SVR) tuned by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), the Genetic Algorithm (GA), Bayesian Optimization (BO), and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for predicting permeate conductivity in a trihybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis pilot plant. Seventy-three published observations of five operating variables, covering about 55 days, were used. All preprocessing and tuning relied on training data only. The models were tested under random, blocked, and chronological validation and compared with default SVR, multiple linear regression, random forest, the training mean, and persistence. Persistence, which uses the last measured value, gave the lowest testing error in every scheme (RMSE 26.6–34.0 µS/cm). No tuned model showed a statistically supported improvement over default SVR. Moving from random to chronological testing raised the RMSE of the tuned models from 44 to 47 to 61–69 µS/cm. In the chronological test, the tuned models over-predicted permeate conductivity by 33–39 µS/cm on average, consistent with sensitivity to temperature values outside the training range. Permutation feature importance (PFI) changed with the validation scheme, and a residual-based uncertainty model underestimated the testing errors. Within the high-pressure period, the five inputs showed weak linear correlations with permeate conductivity, and none of the tested models extracted useful predictive skill from them. Hyperparameter optimization therefore did not improve forward prediction for the dataset. Time-aware validation and simple reference models should be standard in the evaluation of data-driven models for membrane plants. Additional process variables and prospective validation are needed before such models can support real-time operation.

papers.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics for Membrane-Based Gas Separation Systems: Recent Advances, Critical Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is recognized for optimizing transport pathways in membrane-based gas separation systems by visualizing flow behavior, pressure distributions, concentration polarization, and mass transfer. CFD has contributed to the design and improved performance of membranes used in carbon capture, hydrogen purification, natural gas sweetening, biogas upgrading, and oxygen improvement. This review examines recent advances in CFD applications for membrane-based gas separation technologies, including transport equations, numerical modelling strategies, turbulence models, Multiphysics coupling, and membrane module geometries commonly used in CFD, which are hollow fiber, flat-sheet, spiral-wound, and tubular membrane configurations. Recent developments in artificial intelligence-assisted CFD, machine-learning optimization, digital twin concepts, and high-performance computing are discussed to improve predictive capability and computational efficiency. The review also recognizes the current limitations of CFD modelling, including model validation, computational cost, uncertainty quantification, and the representation of complex membrane fouling and aging phenomena. Finally, future research directions are proposed to fill the gap between laboratory-scale simulations and industrial implementation through integrated experimental validation, data-driven modelling, and advanced multiscale simulation frameworks, which provide researchers and engineers with the development of next-generation membrane gas separation systems and highlight future opportunities to acquire energy-efficient, reliable, and sustainable gas separation processes.

papers.title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

papers.title: Engagement and collaboration: evidence from a pedagogical intervention on perceived learning and retention in Brazilian public high schools
papers.abstract: Retention in public high school requires understanding how pedagogical experiences can strengthen students’ ties to school. This article analyzes the relationships among engagement, collaboration, perceived learning, and interest in further education within an intervention based on active learning and educational robotics. The quantitative study uses data from an anonymous evaluative survey administered to public school students participating in a university extension project, resulting in 314 valid responses. The scales showed satisfactory internal consistency, and data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, comparison tests and linear regressions. Results indicate that engagement and collaboration predict perceived learning, and that engagement is associated with interest in further education. The findings suggest that participatory pedagogical interventions can enhance school experience and inform retention strategies in basic education.

papers.title: Trustworthy DINOv2-based skin lesion classification with uncertainty quantification and robust learning from limited medical images
papers.abstract: Abstract Developing reliable automated medical image classification systems remains challenging because annotated medical datasets are often limited, lesion categories are highly imbalanced, and high-confidence errors can occur even when conventional classification performance is strong. This study presents a reliability-oriented skin lesion classification framework based on pretrained DINOv2 representations, Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) feature refinement, a lightweight multilayer perceptron classifier, and uncertainty-aware inference. DINOv2 is used as a pretrained visual backbone, while the downstream classification components are trained in a supervised manner on a lesion-disjoint partition of the HAM10000 dataset. Monte Carlo Dropout is employed during inference to quantify predictive uncertainty and support selective prediction, while post-hoc temperature scaling is used for probability calibration. On the fixed 992-image test set, the representative DINOv2 + MHSA configuration achieved an accuracy of 82.96%, weighted F1-score of 0.8342, macro F1-score of 0.7502, macro AUC of 0.9601, and weighted AUC of 0.9551. Comparisons with ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16, Swin-Tiny, and EfficientNet-B0 provided additional context for conventional classification performance. The reliability analysis showed that uncertainty-based error detection achieved an AUROC of 0.8293 and risk–coverage analysis obtained an AURC of 0.0502. Temperature scaling reduced the Expected Calibration Error from 0.0911 to 0.0369, while the Brier Score decreased from 0.2651 to 0.2467. The MHSA ablation showed improved feature-space organization and ranking-based discrimination, although threshold-dependent classification metrics did not improve uniformly. Limited-data experiments further examined performance when only 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% of the training data were available. Overall, the study evaluates DINOv2-based skin lesion classification from both predictive and reliability perspectives and emphasizes uncertainty estimation, calibration, selective prediction, representation analysis, and data efficiency rather than claiming uniformly superior classification accuracy.

papers.title: SŌRYŪN-Λ: Active Reference Normalization for Recursive Self-Improvement - Exact Observability, Nonlinear Nuisance Cancellation, and Capability-Preserving Recursive Self-Instrumentation
papers.abstract: SŌRYŪN-Λ develops a constructive mathematical approach to recursive capability acquisition: an agent uses variables it has already recovered to change the conditions under which it discovers additional variables. The central mechanism is active reference normalization. Previously acquired measurements become feedback conditions for reversible controls, which bring known coordinates into agreement with a reference state. On this normalized set, otherwise arbitrary nonlinear interference cancels, revealing a new coordinate without requiring identification of the interference law. The research addresses a distinction between learning an observation model and making an observation interpretable through intervention. For a measurement of the form e = z ⊕ F(u), an unrestricted Boolean nuisance function F can have an exponentially large truth table. If the agent can reversibly match u to an accessible reference while preserving the variable of interest, a comparison with the corresponding reference observation removes the shared nuisance contribution. The next discovery can therefore become possible through better experimental control rather than more complete model identification. The manuscript develops six connected contributions: Reference-fiber sensor construction. Over a finite field, existing measurements define a reference fiber on which recovered coordinates agree with their reference values. A probe whose restriction to this fiber is affine becomes a globally linear operational sensor after adaptive normalization. Every nonzero sensor row constructed by this procedure is independent of the previously certified rows and increases measurement rank by one. The theorem permits nonlinear behavior away from the reference fiber; it does not require the raw observation law to be globally linear. Sequential compilation of growing instruments. A certified coherent tower of measurements and translations can be compiled into a sequential reader without recursively rerunning earlier sensors. Each selected restored raw probe is invoked once at its stage, its output determines the next translation, and the recorded translations can be reversed afterward. This gives an explicit mechanism for avoiding repeated execution costs as the instrument library grows. Discovery of opaque reversible controls. A complete Boolean realization starts with one visible bit, a menu of pure coordinate flips, and a menu of triangular reversible shears containing unrestricted nonlinear functions. The structural forms of the two menus are supplied, while their internal ordering, nonlinear laws, and hidden state values are unknown. Restored intervention tests identify the ordering without hidden-coordinate labels in O(n³) primitive calls and O(n²) observed bits. Exact decoding and matching complexity bounds. After calibration, an arbitrary n-bit target state is decoded relative to the reference using exactly n binary observations and at most n²+n primitive calls, including restoration of the queried state. The manuscript proves an n-observation lower bound and an expected n(n−1)/2 primitive-call lower bound for every exact adaptive decoder through the same interface under uniformly distributed target states. The deployed reader is observation optimal and has asymptotically optimal quadratic action scaling. Calibration and deployment costs are accounted for separately. Identification avoidance against a specified passive architecture. A separate counting theorem shows that exact passive correction for an arbitrary nuisance function on q Boolean variables requires at least 2^q−1 counted calibration bits, even when one anchored value is supplied. Active normalization avoids learning those irrelevant nuisance-table entries by changing the query conditions. This separation concerns the defined passive correction architecture; it does not assert an exponential advantage over all active learning algorithms. Reference transport and continuity of meaning. When the reference changes from r to s, the bridge r ⊕ s translates relative coordinates exactly: x ⊕ s = (x ⊕ r) ⊕ (r ⊕ s). Transporting a specified evaluator through this bridge preserves its answer about the same physical state. Reciprocal consistency relations support disagreement detection across anchors, while retained prefix readers preserve earlier executable capabilities within the certified interface or a verified compatible extension. The RSI contribution is a bounded form of recursive self-instrumentation. An acquired observable enables a new feedback operation; that operation simplifies a later measurement; the resulting observable expands the agent’s available instruments. The reference-continuity mechanism draws conceptual inspiration from the relationship. translating continuity through change into explicit coordinate and evaluator transport. That inspiration is separate from the mathematical evidence. The guarantees depend on stated premises, including suitable reversible controls, nondestructive observation, stationarity, structural promises, and correct inverse execution. Primitive calls are an explicit resource unit; the bounds do not imply that arbitrary nonlinear actuators are inexpensive to implement. The general theorem does not guarantee the existence or efficient discovery of every subsequent eligible probe. For fixed n, the Boolean construction terminates at complete operational observability, and its outer discovery rule remains fixed. This is a theoretical research release containing definitions, algorithms, human-readable proofs, lower bounds, a symbolic worked example, and 14 references. It includes the complete 20-page manuscript and editable LaTeX source, together with citation metadata and structured manuscript indexes. The indexed corpus contains 18 document records covering the abstract, 16 sections including appendices, and references, plus 14 formal-statement records. No empirical benchmark results, machine-checked proofs, or independently verified general neural self-improvement are claimed. Scientific priority for the exact construction remains open to literature assessment. The work is intended for researchers in active observability, control theory, adaptive measurement, program synthesis, continual capability acquisition, and recursive self-improvement. Its principal research opportunity is to identify broader classes of systems in which learned controls can remove the need to model nuisance structure while preserving the meaning and executability of earlier capabilities. papers.title: Parametric Estimation in Censored Life-Testing: A Bayesian MAP Approach for Exponential and Weibull Distributions
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the finite-sample performance of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation for Exponential and Weibull lifetime distributions under Type-II right censoring. Data were simulated from both distributions, with each life-testing experiment ending after a specified number of failures among n units. Estimator performance was assessed using bias, mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) under alternative prior specifications, including calibrated, weakly informative and deliberately misspecified priors. The results indicate that the relative performance of MAP and MLE depends on the quality of prior information and the degree of censoring. For the Weibull distribution, estimation performance also differed between the shape and scale parameters. An illustrative application to ball-bearing fatigue-life observations using their original right-censoring information further demonstrates posterior-mode estimation, prior sensitivity and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) based uncertainty quantification. In summary, the location of the MAP estimate within the region of greatest posterior concentration is consistent with direct numerical maximisation of the joint posterior density.
